views.rationale:
RECOMMENDATION: Keep the May measures in place and reopen a leader-level channel toward the late-June G20, without implementing List 4 or adding further entity-list actions before that meeting. Do not roll back List 3 or delist Huawei as an opening bid after Beijing walked back structural text. Use the existing 25% on ~$250B plus the unused List 4 process as leverage to restore a written, enforceable deal on IP, tech transfer, and enforcement—not as an immediate consumer-goods tax.

SUPPORTING RATIONALE: Threat is moderately elevated, not existential and not an opportunity. After months of reported progress (Feb 24 delay of the List 3 hike; April 3 talks on enforcement language), the US on May 5 accused China of trying to renegotiate and raised List 3 from 10% to 25% on May 10; China answered by lifting rates on its ~$60B US list (many effective June 1). That is a real hit to US farm and machinery exporters already on China’s target list, not a free option: soybeans hit decade lows, a second farm-aid package of $16B was announced, and Business Roundtable/Chamber warned the incidence falls on US firms and consumers. Markets are pricing a growth scare: the 10-year yield fell to 2.12% on June 5 (about −73 bp in the window) and the 2-year to 1.83%, below fed funds (~2.38%). Overlaying the May 16 Huawei Entity List (Google/chip pauses) with Xi’s May 20 rare-earth visit and China’s May 31 “unreliable entity list” raises a second-order tech/supply-chain risk to US semiconductor and handset firms if we escalate again immediately. This is below the +0.5 “high” anchor because List 4 (~$300B, phones/apparel/toys) is only proposed (hearing June 17), some economists still call near-term US GDP effects modest, and China’s May factory PMI/export orders are already contracting—so Beijing is under at least as much pressure. Action should therefore stay at hold/negotiate, not further escalate: firing List 4 or widening export controls before Osaka would tax US consumers, invite rare-earth or unreliable-list retaliation, and close the only scheduled off-ramp (Trump/Kudlow have pointed to a possible Trump–Xi meeting at the G20; no working-level round is set). Concession or purchase-only deals are also wrong: US officials said China backtracked on law-change/enforcement language, so rolling back now would ratify that tactic. Negotiate without new commitments; keep current tariffs and the Huawei listing as the price of a resumed text.
key_factors: May collapse after alleged Chinese backtracking on structural/legal commitments
List 3 already at 25% on ~$200B; List 4 (~$300B consumer goods) proposed but not in force
Huawei Entity List plus China unreliable-entity list and rare-earth signaling
Farm-belt retaliation and a second (~$16B) aid package; soybean prices at decade lows
Treasury rally (10y 2.12%, 2y 1.83%) signaling a growth scare
Possible Trump-Xi G20 Osaka meeting as the live diplomatic off-ramp

sources_cited.excerpt: Trump tweets negotiations going too slowly and China attempting to renegotiate; orders List 3 raised to 25% on May 10 and preparation of tariffs on remaining ~$300B.
List 3 tariff rate rises from 10% to 25%.
China announces it will raise retaliatory tariff rates on its ~$60B US-goods list (many effective June 1).
US Commerce Department adds Huawei and affiliates to the Entity List.
Google suspends Huawei Android/GMS access; US chip suppliers pause sales; Xi visits a rare-earth facility in Jiangxi.
China announces an unreliable entity list targeting foreign firms that cut supplies for non-commercial reasons.
Intensive Washington talks report progress on text including enforcement language; no final deal signed.
US 10-year Treasury yield latest 2.12% on 2019-06-05, down 0.73 pp (~26%) over the window.
US 2-year yield latest 1.83% on 2019-06-05, below fed funds (~2.38%).
Talks end without a deal; USTR ordered to begin process of tariffs on remaining ~$300B; China said unwilling to concede on principle issues.
Administration announces $16B farm aid; China had bought about one-third of US soybeans; prices slump so some growers lose money on every acre.
No new talks scheduled; Morgan Stanley warned a lasting breakdown with tariffs on all bilateral trade could push toward recession.
Proposed List 4 covers ~$300B including consumer lines; hearing June 17; excludes pharma, rare earths, critical minerals.
Kudlow: strong possibility Trump and Xi meet at Osaka G20; no other fresh rounds of talks scheduled.
China official May manufacturing PMI deeper contraction; export orders sub-index 46.5 vs 49.2 in April.
